prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. High-fidelity flat screenshot of a real desktop software collaboration app named Console Connect, landscape 1600 by 1000 approximately. Render only the application interface, edge to edge, no laptop, no perspective, no poster. Precise mature developer tool design for long coding sessions: graphite charcoal surfaces, warm ivory readable type, restrained pale chartreuse primary actions, hairline separators, subtly rounded 5px controls, generous but productive spacing. Clear sans-serif UI, monospace only for code and branch names. Authored thin line icons. No gradients, no neon glows, no oversized marketing headline. This is a proposed design using illustrative task data, not a live screenshot.
Product truth: people work locally with their own AI subscriptions; assignments require recipient approval; outputs are drafts until submitted; review acceptance is separate from GitHub merge; terminal sharing is optional and view-only. Brand header Console Connect. Workspace example "Acme / web-app". People Alex, Sam, Jordan. Tools Claude Code, Codex CLI, Antigravity. Realistic task examples "Build login flow", "Review session expiry", "Document auth decisions". Selected task "Build login flow", assigned to "Sam", status "Ready to start", tool "Codex CLI". Main action "Start local session". Repository branch "task/login-flow". A terminal panel showing a prompt and no AI already running on an unapproved task. Small sharing control "Private · Share view". Discussion from Alex: "Keep the existing session timeout." and Sam: "I will include the verification results." Review package fields summary, changes, verification, open questions, state "Draft · only you". Task navigation, team member list, connection label "Connected · Computer host". All text must be coherent and legible. Composition C: team board. Slim left workspace navigation with team presence. Main center is a compact kanban board with columns Inbox, In progress, Review, each with realistic tasks. The selected Build login flow opens in a large right-hand detail pane (about 45 percent of app width) with assignee approval state, Start local session action, terminal area, and discussion. Board foregrounds team progress, right pane preserves hands-on work. Status counts are modest functional labels, never hero metrics.
